rv.q: This dame makes a hell of a Queen.

Instead of a plodding chronological procession we’re treated to a cleverly woven series of sketches. We don’t see the full dirty dozen PMs who’ve had audiences with the Queen, but the eight here include Gordon Kennedy’s clumsy and passionate Gordon Brown, David Calder’s stern Churchill and Nicholas Woodeson’s folksy Harold Wilson.
As is the Queen's astonishing, ovationworthy staying-power.
Happily, Zeldin 's script is also very funny: understated but wincingly convincing in the manner of the best TV mockumentaries.
The problem really is Morgan's blandly amusing but desperately trivial script.
Kristin Scott Thomas succeeds on the throne with her own special brand of twinkling irony and glacial dignity.

cn.t: Critics praise this enthralling royal drama, with Kristin Scott Thomas delivering a fascinating, credible performance as the Queen that proves her a worthy successor to Helen Mirren in Peter Morgan's smart, entertaining play.
